title: High-resolution intravital imaging of the murine hypothalamus using GRIN lenses and confocal microscopy
protocol: Choose the appropriate length for the guide tube.
Fabricate the upper mounting and lower implant sections of the guide tube.
Glue the upper mounting section tip-to-tip with the lower implant section.
Mount the compound guide tube into the stereotaxic arm holder via the upper section.
Detach the upper section upon tube implantation.
Cut two pieces of thin-walled capillary glass tubing for implantation and mounting sections.
Mark cut positions on the tubing with a diamond scriber under a stereomicroscope.
Scratch all around the perimeter of the tubing at the marked positions using a diamond scriber.
Bend the tubing by hand until it breaks at the marked position.
Note which side corresponds to the "broken" side for future assembly.
Polish the bottom tip of the section that will be inserted into the brain with sanding paper.
Clean the polished tip with sterile water and/or compressed air duster.
Cut a small disk (1.8–2.0 mm in diameter) from an 80-130 μm cover glass for sealing.
Trim extra glass from the disk using forceps to create a cover glass disk.
Inspect disk surface under stereomicroscope for scratches or dust.
Discard disk if dust cannot be removed completely.
Seal polished tip of guide tube with cover glass disk.
Apply small amount of UV light-activatable glue onto rim of polished tip using fine applicator.
Position cover glass right above capillary tip and place it on the glue-coated tip.
Ensure glue is not spreading along inner walls or further onto cover glass; discard if necessary.
Proceed with glue curing by UV light for 15–20 seconds.
Remove any protruding portions of cover glass using sanding paper.
Glue implantation and mounting sections of guide tube together tip-to-tip.
Align both parts under stereomicroscope.
Apply thin layer of white craft glue to outer surfaces where two pieces will be joined, ensuring glue does not seep into tubing.
Ensure the glue completely dries before proceeding.
Rinse guide tube with 70% ethanol.
Wait at least 12 hours before proceeding.
Cut a circular piece from standard printing paper twice the diameter of the guide tube.
Make two perpendicular incisions at the center of the paper circle to form a collar.
Slip the collar over the guide tube with the cut corners facing upwards.
Ensure the pedestal moves along the vertical axis but remains in position on the guide tube.
Store fabricated guide tubes in sterile 6-well plates until further use.
Anesthetize mouse by intraperitoneal injections of ketamine/xylazine cocktail.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to eyes.
Shave most dorsal portion of mouse head.
Disinfect the exposed area with betadine.
Place anesthetized mouse in surgical stereotaxic frame.
Keep animal on a heating blanket during surgery.
Make skin incisions at midline ∼1 cm in length using a scalpel.
Secure the skin with surgical clamps.
Remove periosteum with a cotton swab damped in 0.9% saline solution.
Conduct circular craniotomy above the area of interest using a microdrill.
Ensure drill hole diameter exceeds guide tube diameter by 20%-25%.
Remove dura using forceps.
Stop bleeding with triangular-shaped cotton absorption swab if needed.
Stereotaxically position the blunt-tip syringe needle over the area of interest.
Lower the tip into the brain parenchyma down to 0.5 mm above the area of interest.
Pull the syringe plunger until the piston’s distal edge meets the 0.1 mL mark.
Slowly lift the stereotaxic arm holding the needle at approximately 0.5 mm/s.
Once the needle exits the brain, aspirate the parenchymal tissue column into the syringe barrel due to negative pressure.
If aspiration is insufficient, repeat aspiration until all of the desired tissue is removed.
Rinse drill hole with 0.9% saline if more than one aspiration cycle is required.
Remove excess fluids/blood with a triangular absorption swab.
Apply a small amount of instant adhesive at the bottom side of the pedestal.
Be careful not to apply glue to the guide tube itself.
Stereotaxically lower the guide tube into the aspirated path.
Depress pedestal/collar onto the skull once the guide tube reaches the desired coordinates.
Allow for the glue to dry completely.
Apply a small amount of instant glue between each of the four corners of the pedestal and the guide tube wall.
Gently press corners against the wall.
Apply a thin layer of dental cement on top of the pedestal.
Let the dental cement harden completely.
Using a stereomicroscope, carefully peel off the clear glue film where the tube sections connect using a sharp needle tip.
Gently lift and remove the mounting section.
Apply one more layer of dental cement to fully secure the guide tube implant.
Be careful to not let any dental cement enter the inside of the tube.
Seal the top of the implant with reusable adhesive or tape to prevent debris from entering into tube.
Clip extra skin around the guide tube if necessary.
Administer carprofen.
Place mouse in a cage kept on a heating blanket while recovering from anesthesia.
Inject 1 mL of warm (37°C) sterile saline subcutaneously to prevent dehydration.
Anesthetize mouse by intraperitoneal injection of a ketamine-xylazine cocktail.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to eyes to prevent drying during the imaging session.
Place and secure anesthetized mouse in holding frame (Kopf) to be positioned underneath objective.
Keep animal on a heating blanket during the imaging session.
Position the mouse head under the dissecting microscope.
Carefully remove the protective seal/adhesive that covers the top of the guide tube with forceps.
Focus on the bottom of the guide tube and adjust the head position of the mouse so that when looking down through both eyepieces simultaneously, the bottom of the guide tube forms an oval.
Inspect the tube inner wall and the cover glass for dust particles using the stereomicroscope.
If necessary, inject H2O using 1 mL insulin syringe.
Dry with absorbing tissue (Kimwipes).
Take extra caution when rinsing the guide tube to prevent damage to the cover glass at the tube bottom.
Inject fluorescein-isothiocyanate dextran intravenously into mouse tail vein immediately prior to imaging session (optional).
Attach GRIN lens holder to microscope.
Slip holder cuff without the disk onto the 20× objective and tighten holder screw.
For low magnification, insert 1.4 mm GRIN lens in inverted direction through central bore of custom-fabricated plastic disc.
Insert disc into holder and secure with clips.
Position upper tip of GRIN lens so that distance to the objective equals sum of objective’s and GRIN lens’ focal plane distances.
Reverse the orientation of the GRIN lens to change magnification.
Employ a 0.7 mm GRIN lens for different magnifications.
Use ∼480/520 nm excitation/emission filters for fluorescein-conjugated dextran imaging.
Use ∼555/580 nm excitation/emission filters for tdTomato protein imaging.
Acquire images at a resolution of 512 × 512 pixels with scan speeds of 0.5–1 pixels/μs.
Set the pinhole size to 2–14 airy units using ZEN software.
Use the lowest possible laser power to minimize tissue damage.
Position the stereotaxic imaging frame under the GRIN lens aligned with the guide tube.
Lower the objective-GRIN lens assembly into the guide tube until a fluorescence signal is detectable.
Further lower the assembly until the desired imaging area is reached.
Allow movement of the GRIN lens along the vertical axis in the lens holder.
Maximize the effective field of view by altering the X-Y position of the GRIN lens within the guide tube using the microscope stage.
Visualize the vasculature by i.v. injection of fluorescent dextran to track individual cells over time.
Lift the objective-GRIN lens assembly after imaging is completed.
Replace the GRIN lens with a different lens if necessary.
Re-seal the guide tube with protective adhesive at the end of the imaging session.
Return the animal to its home cage placed on a heating blanket until full recovery from anesthesia.
